zh.title: AI脑波英语学习舱完整流程：孩子进来以后到底怎么学？
zh.description: AI脑波英语学习舱不是让孩子躺一躺就会，而是通过测评、读熟、进舱节律化输入、出舱检测、错词复现和专项训练，把词汇转化为听力、阅读、写作和考试可调用能力。
zh.lead: AI脑波英语学习舱的重点不是“躺着就会”，而是先测评、再读熟、进舱做节律化输入、出舱马上检测，最后把词汇接到听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘上。

sections.h2: 为什么要先把流程讲清楚？
paragraphs: 很多家长第一次听到“脑波英语”会天然怀疑：这是不是玄学？真正能打消怀疑的，不是更多口号，而是把孩子从进校区到出舱检测的每一步讲清楚。
AI脑波英语对外展示时，应该先讲“怎么学、怎么测、怎么复现”，再解释特定频率声波和非侵入式学习舱。这样家长更容易理解：学习舱只是关键环节之一，真正交付的是一套训练闭环。
bullets: 不先讲神奇效果，先讲测评和训练动作
不只展示设备，必须展示教练、词表、检测和错词记录
不把词汇当终点，而是解释它如何支持听力、阅读、写作和刷卷

sections.h2: 第一步：30分钟测评先看孩子卡在哪里
paragraphs: 到店后不建议一上来就推长期课程。更稳的方式是先做测评，了解孩子的音标、自然拼读、词汇量、听力反应、阅读卡点和最近考试表现。
测评的意义是把问题拆开：有的孩子是不会读，有的是词汇量不足，有的是会背但听不出来、阅读里认不快。没有测评，就很难判断先补什么。
bullets: 音标与自然拼读是否过关
核心词汇是否能读、能认、能拼写
听力和阅读的真实卡点在哪里
是否适合先做3次体验课

sections.h2: 第二步：进舱前必须先读熟、认熟、拼写过
paragraphs: 学习舱训练不是让孩子直接躺进去听。进舱前，教练要先带孩子把本次词表读熟、认熟，并完成必要的拼写动作。
因为不会读的词，很难真正记住；读不准的词，也会影响后面的听力反应和阅读识别。AI脑波英语强调“记住多少比背多少更重要”，所以进舱前的准备不能省。
bullets: 跟读并大声朗读，先保证发音
遮挡英文做默写或拼写练习
把本次词表从陌生变成熟悉，再进入学习舱

sections.h2: 第三步：学习舱里做什么？
paragraphs: 孩子进入学习舱后，戴上眼罩和耳机，通过特定频率声波和课程音频，在更安静、更专注的状态里完成节律化输入。
训练动作不是睡觉，而是“听中文想英文、听英文想中文、听拼写用手空书”。这一步的目标，是让单词的声音、拼写和意思反复绑定。
bullets: 戴眼罩耳机，降低外部干扰
通过耳机完成非侵入式声音输入
配合课程内容完成词汇复现动作
教练在外部观察和管理训练节奏

sections.h2: 第四步：出舱检测决定家长是否能看见效果
paragraphs: AI脑波英语最重要的信任点之一，是出舱后马上检测。孩子到底记住了多少，哪些词还不稳，不能靠感觉，要靠汉译英、英译汉、拼写和错词记录看出来。
对家长来说，出舱检测比任何宣传语都更重要。因为它把“孩子是否真的记住”变成了可观察、可记录、可复盘的结果。
bullets: 汉译英看输出
英译汉看识别
拼写看准确性
错词本看后续复习重点

sections.h2: 为什么词汇突破会影响听力、阅读、写作和刷卷？
paragraphs: 家长容易误解：单词可以自己背，为什么要专门训练？关键在于，考试需要的不是“背过”，而是“可调用”。
词汇能调用以后，听力能抓关键词，阅读能看懂句子，写作时脑子里有词，刷卷复盘也能真正定位问题。AI脑波英语把词汇突破作为地基，再接语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷。
bullets: 听力：声音和意思反应更快
阅读：文章不再被大量陌生词卡住
写作：表达时有词可用
刷卷：错题能回到词汇、语法和题型上复盘

paragraphs: 9.9元3次课不是为了让家长马上买长期课，而是让家长看见孩子是否适合、是否愿意配合、训练后能否复现。
每节约2小时，家长可以重点看四件事：孩子进舱前是否能读熟，本次词表出舱后能否复现，错词是否被记录，教练是否能讲清下一步训练安排。
bullets: 看孩子是否愿意进入训练状态
看出舱检测是否有记录
看错词是否有复习安排
看家长是否真正理解后续路径

faqs.q: AI脑波英语是不是孩子躺着就会？
faqs.a: 不是。学习舱只是训练环节之一，完整流程包括测评、读熟、进舱节律化输入、出舱检测、错词复现和后续专项训练。

faqs.q: 为什么要先做出舱检测？
faqs.a: 因为检测能把“是否记住”变成可观察结果。汉译英、英译汉、拼写和错词记录能帮助家长和教练判断本次训练是否有效。

faqs.q: 学习舱训练和听力、阅读有什么关系？
faqs.a: 词汇如果能被快速听出、认出和调用，就会支撑听力关键词捕捉、阅读理解和写作输出。词汇训练不是终点，而是英语提分的地基。
主要看孩子是否适合训练、是否愿意配合、出舱后能否复现词汇，以及教练是否能给出清楚的后续学习路径。

zh.cta: 如果孩子背单词总忘、阅读看不懂、听力反应慢，可以先预约30分钟测评，再体验9.9元3次课，看见训练过程和出舱检测结果后再决定是否进入系统学习。

en.title: What Happens Inside an AI English Learning Cabin? A Step-by-Step Process
en.description: AI Brainwave English explains the full learning cabin workflow: assessment, pronunciation preparation, cabin-based rhythmic input, exit testing, error review and how vocabulary supports listening, reading, writing and exam practice.
en.lead: An AI English learning cabin should not be presented as a magic shortcut. The credible process starts with assessment, pronunciation preparation, rhythmic audio input, immediate exit testing and review that connects vocabulary to listening, reading, writing and exam practice.

sections.h2: Why should the process be explained before the technology?
paragraphs: When parents or education partners first hear the phrase “brainwave English”, many of them naturally ask whether it is real or exaggerated. The most credible answer is to show the process instead of relying on slogans.

AI Brainwave English should be understood as a structured training workflow. The learning cabin is an important input environment, but the full service includes assessment, preparation, testing, review and follow-up instruction.
bullets: Start with assessment instead of claims
Show the coach, word list, testing sheet and review record
Explain vocabulary as a foundation for usable English ability

sections.h2: Step 1: A 30-minute assessment identifies the real gap
paragraphs: Before recommending a training path, the center checks pronunciation, phonics, vocabulary level, listening response, reading obstacles and recent exam performance.

The purpose is to separate different problems. Some learners cannot pronounce words accurately; some lack vocabulary volume; others can memorize words but cannot recognize them quickly in listening and reading.
bullets: Pronunciation and phonics
Core vocabulary recognition and spelling
Listening and reading bottlenecks
Whether a short trial is a good first step

sections.h2: Step 2: Students prepare the word list before entering the cabin
paragraphs: The student does not simply lie down and listen. Before the cabin session, the coach helps the student read, recognize and spell the target words.
This preparation matters because words that cannot be pronounced accurately are harder to retain and harder to use in listening or reading tasks.
bullets: Read aloud with accurate pronunciation
Practice spelling and recognition
Move from unfamiliar words to a prepared input list

sections.h2: Step 3: The learning cabin provides focused rhythmic input
paragraphs: Inside the cabin, the student wears an eye mask and headphones. The goal is to reduce distraction and create a calmer, more focused input state through structured audio.
The student is still actively participating: hearing Chinese and recalling English, hearing English and recalling meaning, and using finger-writing movements during spelling cues.
bullets: Non-invasive headphone-based audio input
Reduced visual distraction
Vocabulary meaning, sound and spelling are repeatedly linked
The coach manages the session from outside the cabin

sections.h2: Step 4: Exit testing makes the result observable
paragraphs: The most important trust point is what happens after the session. The student immediately completes Chinese-to-English, English-to-Chinese, spelling and error-record tasks.
This turns the question “Did the student really remember it?” into something observable, recorded and reviewable.
bullets: Chinese-to-English output
English-to-Chinese recognition
Spelling accuracy
Error list for follow-up review

sections.h2: How does vocabulary training support exam performance?
paragraphs: The goal is not to memorize isolated word meanings. The goal is usable vocabulary: words that students can hear, recognize, spell, recall and apply in exam contexts.
When vocabulary becomes usable, listening keywords become easier to catch, reading comprehension becomes less blocked, writing has more available language, and exam review becomes more precise.
bullets: Listening: faster sound-to-meaning response
Reading: fewer blocked sentences
Writing: more words available for expression
Exam practice: errors can be traced back to vocabulary, grammar or question type

sections.h2: What should parents or partners look for in a short trial?
paragraphs: A short trial should not be judged by excitement alone. Parents and partners should check whether the student cooperates, whether the word list is tested after the session, whether errors are recorded, and whether the coach can explain the next step clearly.
For education centers, this same process can also help evaluate whether a learning cabin project has a repeatable parent-consultation and delivery model.
bullets: Student cooperation
Exit-test records
Error-review plan
Clear next-step recommendation

faqs.q: Is the AI English learning cabin a passive listening session?
faqs.a: No. It includes preparation before the session, structured audio input inside the cabin, and immediate exit testing and review afterwards.
Exit testing makes vocabulary retention observable. It checks recognition, output, spelling and errors instead of relying on a vague feeling that the session worked.

faqs.q: How does vocabulary training help listening and reading?
faqs.a: When a word can be quickly heard, recognized and recalled, it becomes more useful in listening comprehension, reading comprehension, writing and exam review.

faqs.q: Can education centers use this process for a pilot?
faqs.a: Yes. A pilot can use assessment, short trial sessions, exit testing and parent feedback to validate demand, delivery quality and conversion before wider rollout.

en.cta: Parents can book an assessment to understand the student’s starting point. Education partners can use the same workflow to evaluate whether an AI English learning cabin pilot is suitable for their center.
